page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor. This x86_64 architecture system features 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per physical core. The instance includes a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps but does not feature any local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory performance, with large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching 210.08 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 98.02 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% tier. PassMark CPU and memory scores are also strong, registering at 49425.07 and 2940.23 respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression is highly efficient at 31.99 GB/sec. However, text generation performance for large language models is weak to poor, with a 7B model generating only 7.8 tokens per second, reflecting the lack of GPU acceleration for deep learning workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the x2iezn.metal offers high resource density for memory-bound enterprise applications, though the absence of local storage requires reliance on external block storage. This server is optimized for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise applications requiring high-frequency single-core execution alongside massive RAM capacity.
